Which do you prefer: sequential based exit numbering or distance-based exit numbering?
I'm only used to the sequential system. How would a distance based system even look?
Exit numbers are based off of the mile/kilometer the exit is located on in a distance-based system.
I prefer the sequential system then since I don't see the value in the other system.

Well when you have a distance based system, it makes it easier to calculate how far it is between two exits and lets you have a better gauge of where the exit is. It is also easier to give a new exit a number when it's in a distance based system than a sequential one.

To further that point the U.S. interstate system uses the mile marker based system.

Pennsylvania is 308 miles wide. So heading west out of New York the first exit in Penn is exit 308. Before they changed to this system that exit was 140 or something.

ok so before it was 140 but you have no way of knowing how long until the next exit. Though you do know there are 139 exits left in the state. But you don't know that the next exit (exit 302) is 6 miles away.

This is even more dramatic in Wyoming or Nebraska where exit 1 and exit 2 might be 50 miles apart.

State highways can use whatever system they want. But interstates fall into federal regulations and to keep all interstates uniform they went with the mile marker system

As a former truck driver this was a blessing. going state to state was confusing enough w/o having to figure out their exit numbering system.
I think a distance based system is better than sequential. You can have a rough idea of how far away your exit is.
